findings.claim: The new pin covers only the scope half of the tree-ambiguity rule: it requires "more than one commit carries it, the anchor is ambiguous". The consequence clause ": t1 is omitted and the ambiguity is disclosed, never resolved by position" (closure-feedback.md:40) has no pin. An edit that keeps the pinned prefix but changes the consequence still passes the test. One example is "...the anchor is ambiguous: t1 is taken from the earliest carrier". This weakens S9's requirement that an inverted clause must still be caught, for the rule this commit rewrote. To fix it, extend the required clause through "t1 is omitted and the ambiguity is disclosed, never resolved by position".

The SKILL.md closure sentence this commit edits, "When the anchor is ambiguous, omit t1; never resolved by position.", has no pin in the closure-section requireClauses (test lines 113-116). Deleting it, or inverting it to resolve by position, would not fail the test. The edit also dropped the subject ("it is"), so the second clause no longer says what is "never resolved". The pin gap existed before this commit. The unpinned edit to the clause makes it more visible.

Removing "on the default branch" leaves "more than one commit carries it" without any commit set: all refs, reachable from a given head, or including unreachable objects. Owner decision (3) says to count every commit carrying the tree. Without a stated enumeration, such as all commits reachable from any ref, an executor can reasonably search only the current branch's history. That search can find one carrier where the repository has several, and the anchor would then be treated as unambiguous. The failure is the false certainty that the old branch scope had, and that this commit meant to remove.
